standard.title: Produce works for/challenging audiences
standard.description: apply production processes and use media arts concepts to construct representations and produce media arts works that communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning, and confirm or challenge the expectations of specific audiences
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can design media arts works using pre-production processes. They can apply genre conventions deliberately. They have not yet produced works that specifically confirm or challenge audience expectations — applying full production processes with critical awareness of how representations position audiences.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students apply production processes and media arts concepts to produce media arts works that communicate ideas, perspectives and/or meaning, and confirm or challenge the expectations of specific audiences.

nodes.label: Production to confirm or challenge expectations
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply production processes to produce a media arts work — making deliberate choices about whether to confirm or challenge genre conventions and audience expectations, and explaining how each choice serves this intent.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce one media arts work that either confirms or challenges at least two audience expectations — documenting the production choices made and explaining how each serves the intended relationship with the audience.
nodes.typical_width: Produce media arts works across forms (silent film, music video, stop motion, animation, genre film) using full production processes; use mise-en-scène, camera work, sound, editing and media technologies in genre-typical or genre-disrupting ways; apply ethical, legal and cultural safety considerations; evaluate how production choices position audiences.
wider: Produce a genre film that either conforms to or deliberately challenges the conventions of its genre — documenting the production decisions made and evaluating how each positions the audience, then producing an alternative opening or sequence that takes the opposite approach

Create multiple representations of the same person, place or concept in different media forms and for different intentions — evaluating how each medium, genre choice and audience relationship shapes the representation produced
nodes.hinge_reason: The ability to consciously position production choices in relation to audience expectations is the core capability of this standard — without it, production is competent craft but not critical media practice.

response_modes.reason: Use Viewpoints questions to make the confirmation/challenge decision explicit: 'How does this camera choice confirm what the audience expects? What would happen if I did the opposite?' The reasoning behind each choice is as important as the choice.

success_criteria: Student produces a media arts work making deliberate choices about genre conventions and audience expectations
Student can explain how at least two production choices confirm or challenge those expectations

nodes.label: Ethical and collaborative production
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply ethical, legal and culturally safe production practices — including community collaboration approaches — throughout the production process.
nodes.minimum_width: Apply at least two ethical, legal or culturally safe production practices during a production (e.g. copyright compliance, ICIP protocol, community consultation) and document these applications.
nodes.typical_width: Apply ethical, legal and culturally safe practices throughout production; use Viewpoints questions to evaluate communicative intent during post-production; consider community collaboration protocols when representing local histories or identities; evaluate how production intentions are being communicated at each stage.
wider: Collaborate with a community (using school protocols to contact First Nations Australian or other community groups) to produce a media arts work that explores, challenges or celebrates local histories, cultures or identities — documenting the collaboration process and reflecting on how it shaped the production

Produce a media arts work on a social or cultural issue — applying full ethical, legal and cultural safety review at each production stage, and reflecting on how the issue's sensitivity shaped production decisions

response_modes.reason: Ethical production practice is integrated throughout the production cycle, not a separate compliance step — ensure students treat ethical decisions (community consultation, copyright, ICIP) as production decisions, not administrative requirements.

success_criteria: Student applies at least two ethical, legal or culturally safe production practices and documents them
Student can explain how each practice shaped production decisions
